# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 25 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 25 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_025_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 25

**25:1** Among the priests there arose a great consternation over Zechariah's absence from his appointed duties of service to God. A vessel of water was brought forward and a prayer was offered, that God might reveal what had happened. Lots were then cast, and the lot fell to Simeon.

**25:2** Simeon had been informed by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death until he had first set eyes on the Christ incarnate. When the child was brought to the temple, Simeon saw him and recognized him, and he said: "Lord, now let your servant depart in peace, for my eyes have seen your salvation."

**25:3** It was I, James, who wrote down this history in Jerusalem. And when the tumult arose at the death of Herod, I withdrew into the wilderness until the disturbance had passed, giving glory to the Lord God who bestowed upon me this grace and this wisdom.

**25:4** Peace be to the one who fears the Lord. Amen.

---

*[Scribal colophon — P.Bodmer V:] The Birth of Mary. Revelation of James. Peace to the one who sent it and to the one who reads it.*
